key_insight: The paper evaluates GPT-6-Astra as the core of a robot-control agent on EBench, examining how a frontier multimodal model compares and interacts with specialized robot policies. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so it does not establish which approach performs best.
problem_solved: Understanding the strengths and limitations of general-purpose multimodal models versus post-trained vision-language-action (VLA) and world action model (WAM) policies across robotic manipulation demands.
method: Evaluate GPT-6-Astra on EBench through an agent harness that controls a robot.
Use the same visual and proprioceptive observation protocol as post-trained robot policies to support comparison.
Examine capabilities across manipulation demands and interactions with specialized policies; detailed configurations are not available in the supplied excerpt.
impact: This evaluation could help practitioners decide when to use a general-purpose multimodal agent, a specialized robot policy, or a combination. Performance gains and practical trade-offs cannot be determined from the excerpt.

paper_title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
